correctness.rationale: The source update is substituted exactly. Orthogonal singular coordinates reduce every positive singular value to the matrix \((1+q^2)^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}1&-q\\q&1\end{bmatrix}\), whose squared norm factor is exactly \((1+q^2)^{-1}\). Nullspace projections are invariant because the coupling lies in the corresponding ranges. These facts prove the limit and exact distance formula for all iterations, not merely experimentally.

value.rationale: Bilinear games are the canonical stability test for competitive optimization, and nonunique Nash sets occur naturally when the interaction is rectangular or rank deficient. The result identifies CGD's implicit equilibrium selection exactly: the algorithm removes only active singular components and preserves strategically neutral components. It also quantifies the source claim that stronger interactions help, while showing that the step controls speed and rotation but not the selected equilibrium.
